podcast.title: Record Label Collapse
podcast.body: Greta's promising trajectory was halted by significant turmoil at their record label. Both the presidents of the label and the band's A&R representative, who had been their main champion, were fired. This series of events led to the complete collapse of the band's enterprise. "then the presidents of their record label got fired. Then their A&R guy, the guy who would champion them to the label, also got fired and the whole enterprise collapsed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Isolated Rock Resurgence Post-Trump (2017)
xref.body: Greta Van Fleet is mentioned as an "isolated example" of a rock band that emerged around 2017, at a time when a widespread explosion in loud, angry rock following the election of Donald Trump did not materialize as predicted based on historical patterns. "There were however some isolated examples, like Greta van Fleet. This is from 2017."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

xref.title: Baltimore Band in Alternative Hard Rock Scene
xref.body: Turnstile, a band from Baltimore, was mentioned in the context of new young bands inspired by old school classic rock, contributing to the Alternative Hard Rock scene in the 2010s. They were highlighted alongside Greta Van Fleet and The Struts as examples of this trend. "We should also bring in Baltimore's turn style."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

xref.title: Comparison to Greta Van Fleet
xref.body: In 2017, when Greta Van Fleet emerged, many older listeners (boomers and Gen Xers) immediately noted a strong resemblance to Led Zeppelin's sound from 1971, highlighting a sense of musical déjà vu despite younger listeners perceiving Greta Van Fleet as new and fresh. "But God, didn't Led Zeppelin sound like this in 1971?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)

xref.title: Inspired by Classic Rock
xref.body: Greta Van Fleet was mentioned as a "new young band" clearly inspired by "old school classic rock." Their inspiration came from raiding their parents' classic rock record collections, showcasing a trend of contemporary artists drawing heavily from earlier rock styles. "We talked about Great Event Fleet on a previous episode." "They rated their parents classic rock record collection for their inspiration."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

xref.title: Perception as New vs. Old
xref.body: When Greta Van Fleet emerged in 2017, younger audiences perceived them as "new and fresh." However, older generations, particularly boomers and Gen Xers, immediately drew comparisons to Led Zeppelin's sound from 1971, illustrating a generational divide in musical perception and the phenomenon of musical styles being independently rediscovered. "The kids thought they were new and fresh. But God, didn't Led Zeppelin sound like this in 1971?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
